messages.author: a9413cb4eedc9e12
messages.subject: Getting a stacked barchard
parts:
I have a barchart that looks good to me but I have a request to change
it from a side-by-side chart (which makes the most sense to me) to
stacked

Data consists of sales figures by month for different products for two
divisions of a company

The idea would be to produce stacked bars for the number of products
sold by division by month..

At the moment I'm stumped. Am I missing something obvious or do I
need to reshape my data or what?

Any help would be appreciated.

Simple example of what I've done so far.
===============================

library(ggplot2, reshape2)
df1 <- structure(list(prod = structure(c(1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L,
3L), .Label = c("x",
"y", "z"), class = "factor"), jan = c(10L, 15L, 20L, 20L, 15L,
10L), feb = c(10L, 18L, 10L, 15L, 18L, 10L), march = c(10L, 10L,
34L, 17L, 34L, 18L), group = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L,
2L), .Label = c("a", "b"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("prod",
"jan", "feb", "march", "group"), class = "data.frame", row.names =
c(NA,
-6L))


df2 <- melt(df1,id= c("prod","group"))
str(df2)

p <- ggplot(df2, aes(prod, value, fill=group))
p <- p + facet_grid(.~ variable)
p <- p + geom_bar(stat = "identity", position="dodge") +
xlab("Products") + ylab("Sales") +
opts(title = "Monthly Sales Breakdown") +
scale_fill_discrete('Group')
p

==================================

Just change position = "dodge" to position = "stack" (or get rid of
the position argument altogether, as position = "stack" is the default
for geom_bar().

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Getting a stacked barchard
parts:
Hi:

I was playing around with the idea of using line graphs instead of
stacked bar charts in John Kane's data and ran across a couple of
things that are useful to note (although the graphs aren't that pretty
;)

(1) It's a bad idea to conflate variable names with names of ggplot2
aesthetics; once again, group is a culprit:

> str(df2)
'data.frame': 18 obs. of 4 variables:
$ prod : Factor w/ 3 levels "x","y","z": 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 ...
$ group : Factor w/ 2 levels "a","b": 1 1 1 2 2 2 1 1 1 2 ...
$ variable: Factor w/ 3 levels "jan","feb","march": 1 1 1 1 1 1 2 2 2 2 ...
$ value : int 10 15 20 20 15 10 10 18 10 15 ...

> ggplot(df2, aes(x = variable, y = value, color = prod)) +
+ geom_point(size = 2.5) + geom_line(aes(group = prod), size = 1) +
+ facet_wrap( ~ group, ncol = 1)
Error in names(out) <- names(x) :
'names' attribute [5] must be the same length as the vector [0]

Now change the data by replacing group with gp:

> str(df2)
'data.frame': 18 obs. of 4 variables:
$ prod : Factor w/ 3 levels "x","y","z": 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 ...
$ gp : Factor w/ 2 levels "a","b": 1 1 1 2 2 2 1 1 1 2 ...
$ variable: Factor w/ 3 levels "jan","feb","march": 1 1 1 1 1 1 2 2 2 2 ...
$ value : int 10 15 20 20 15 10 10 18 10 15 ...

# Same code except for name of variable (group -> gp) now works:
> p3 <- ggplot(df2, aes(x = variable, y = value, color = prod)) +
+ geom_point(size = 2.5) + geom_line(aes(group = prod), size = 1) +
+ labs(x = 'Month', y = 'Sales', color = 'Product') +
+ facet_wrap(~ gp, ncol = 1)
> p3
# No error, plot renders (OK, I added a line :)

Message: when using ggplot2, don't use variable names that correspond
to ggplot2 aesthetics, such as group, colo(u)r, fill, shape, etc.,
because it may come back to bite you :) The problem arose because I
used a group aesthetic in the plot call when the data contained a
variable named group. A clash results.

(2) In the labs() statement, color = 'Product' doesn't work, but
colour = 'Product' does (after changing color to colour in the
ggplot() statement as well). Another color/colour infelicity to add to
the list...

FWIW,
Dennis

messages.author: 1e82ea932416652e
messages.subject: Re: Getting a stacked barchard
parts:
John,

Side-by-side bar charts make it difficult to see the pattern of changes in any one variable from month to month, as you have to visually "blank out" the intervening bars. Stacked bar charts have the advantage of showing the total (and I would guess that this is why the stacked version was requested), but make it almost impossible to see or interpret the changes in individual variables from month to month. Because both types of charts hide more data than they show, it's usually a good idea to avoid them. Stephen Few, Edward Tufte and William Cleveland have all written persuasively on the subject, and some of their materials can be found for free online.

Instead of bar charts, you might try line graphs with facets to separate the "a" and "b" groups in one of the panels. Line charts make it easy to compare values within and across groups and months. When you need to also show the combined total, the best approach is to stack a graph for total on top of a graph showing the individual values (this is something like Tufte's "small multiples"). In ggplot, this can be done using viewports.

Starting with your code (replacing "group" with "prodgroup" to avoid namespace conflicts, as pointed out by Dennis), the following produces something close to what I have in mind:

library(ggplot2, reshape2)
df1 <- structure(list(prod = structure(c(1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L,
3L), .Label = c("x",
"y", "z"), class = "factor"), jan = c(10L, 15L, 20L, 20L, 15L,
10L), feb = c(10L, 18L, 10L, 15L, 18L, 10L), march = c(10L, 10L,
34L, 17L, 34L, 18L), group = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L,
2L), .Label = c("a", "b"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("prod",

"jan", "feb", "march", "prodgroup"), class = "data.frame", row.names =
c(NA,
-6L))

df2 <- melt(df1,id= c("prod","prodgroup"))
str(df2)

# create a data frame containing the monthly total sales
m3 <- rowsum(df2$value, df2$variable)
df3 <- data.frame(variable = unique(df2$variable), value = m3)

# generate a line graph of individual sales, colored by product and grouped by "prodgroup"
ind.g <- ggplot() +
    facet_grid(facets = prodgroup ~ .) +
    geom_point(aes(x = variable,y = value,colour = prod),data=df2,alpha = 0.5952) +
    geom_line(aes(x = variable,y = value,colour = prod,group = prod),data=df2)
# generate a line graph of the total sales
sum.g <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(aes(x = variable,y = value),data=df3,alpha = 0.5952) +
    geom_line(aes(x = variable,y = value),data=df3)
# set up a device to plot multiple graphs
png("grid line chart.png", width = 800, height = 600)
grid.newpage()
# create two viewports, one above the other
pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(2,1)))
vplayout <- function(x, y)
    viewport(layout.pos.row = x, layout.pos.col = y)

# print total sales to the top viewport
print(sum.g, vp = vplayout(1,1))
# print individual sales to the bottom viewport
print(ind.g, vp = vplayout(2,1))
#close the device
dev.off()

Note that the above saves the graph as png in the current working directory; it does not display it within R.

With the above, there is a problem with alignment of the months between the top (total sales) panel and the bottom (individual product sales) panel. I can think of two ways to solve this display problem. One approach would be to control the width of the top viewport using the widths= argument. This seems like it would take some finessing to get right. A second approach would be to add the totals in df3 back into df2 using "prodgroup" = "total" and just plot a single graph using facets ("total," "a" and "b"), instead of the two graphs using viewports. Potential pitfalls of this approach are that you would need to control the order of facets using a third variable (as recently discussed in another thread on this discussion list) and that there might be insufficient visual distinction between the "total sales" graph and the other "individual" sales-by-group graphs.
